title: Toileting Readiness (Respectful Care)
strapline: Nappy changes as unhurried conversations, the potty offered without pressure — following each child's own body clock, kindly.
intent: Approach nappies, potties and toilet-learning with respect — the child as a partner in their own care, never a body things are done to.
Build body-awareness so toddlers begin to notice the signs of needing a wee or a poo, at their own developmental pace.
Grow the independence and dignity of self-care — pulling clothes up and down, sitting on the potty, washing hands afterwards.
Support each child's readiness in step with their family, so toilet-learning is calm, consistent and free of pressure or shame.
Turn intimate care into a warm, connecting moment of one-to-one attention, language and trust.
implementation: Make nappy changes a relationship, not a task: tell the child what will happen, go gently, chat and sing, never rush or distract them away from their own body.
Offer the potty or toilet matter-of-factly at natural moments, letting the child accept or decline without any pressure.
Notice and name the signs together — the pause, the wriggle, the tell — so children learn to read their own bodies.
Dress toddlers in easy-to-manage clothes so pulling down and up can become their own job.
Work hand-in-hand with families for consistency, keep every response calm and accident-free of shame, and always follow the child's lead.
key_questions: I'm going to change your nappy now — shall we go together?
Did you feel that? That's your body telling you.
Would you like to try the potty, or not just now?
Can you pull your trousers down all by yourself?
You told me you needed to go — well done for noticing!

impact.text: Toddlers cooperate with nappy changes and begin to notice and signal their own toileting needs.
A child pulls their own clothes up and down and tries the potty themselves — 'me do it!' — with growing pride.
Children anticipate the familiar care routine — nappy time, potty after sleep, hands afterwards — knowing what comes next.
Unhurried, respectful intimate care deepens the bond between child and key person, comforted and safe.

enhancements: A calm, private changing area with the child's own things and time built in for talk.
A potty and low toilet step so children can manage the whole business themselves.
Books and dolls about using the potty for unpressured, playful familiarity.
Easy-manage clothes — elastic waists, no fiddly fastenings — during toilet-learning.
A shared home-nursery record so families and key persons keep the approach consistent.

playing_exploring: Children explore toilet-learning playfully — through books, dolls and unpressured tries.
Body signals are noticed and named together, at the child's own pace.
active_learning: Toddlers take growing pride in managing more of their own care, wanting to do it themselves.
creating_thinking: Children begin to link the feeling in their body to what comes next, and act on it in time.
